clue.text: Eminent physiologist, big noise pocketing cash

indicators.note: the big noise puts the cash in its pocket, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a bang is a big noise
tin is slang for money or cash

explanation.surface: A loud and wealthy scientist stuffs his pockets with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Banting was the Canadian physiologist who shared the Nobel Prize for the discovery of insulin.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Banting is a famous physiologist, co-discoverer of insulin, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Intelligent individual wants alarm put in old train

parts.note: bright means clever or intelligent

indicators.note: put in means the alarm word goes inside the individual word

parts.note: one is a single individual
a bell gives an alarm

explanation.surface: A clever person wants an alarm fitted on an old train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brighton Belle was a Pullman express running between London and Brighton until 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brighton Belle was a named luxury train, withdrawn in 1972, so it is an old train.

clue.text: Name old record with melody that's in Holst's suite

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A music lover names an old record with a tune from a Holst suite.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst's orchestral suite 'The Planets' has a movement for each planet, Neptune the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Mystic, is the final movement of Holst's suite The Planets.

clue.text: Erupt when rugby is this unskilful!

definitions.text: Erupt when rugby is this unskilful!

parts.words: Erupt when rugby is this unskilful!
parts.note: the word erupt contains RU, the rugby abbreviation; replace those two letters with the opening letters of a word meaning unskilful and the rest of erupt rearranged gives that word

explanation.surface: Fans explode in fury when the rugby is this clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: ERUPT is RU plus EPT rearranged; the answer is IN plus EPT. So the clue says the answer is what you get from erupt when RU is IN. 'unskilful' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, clumsy or incompetent, a straightforward synonym for unskilful.

clue.text: Travel on railway route it's when that can be saved

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second
it's, read as it has, means the travel word holds the when word inside it

parts.note: to go is to travel
as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
a railway line is a route

explanation.surface: A traveller on a train line points out the time when fuel can be saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' reads as 'it has': the travel word holds the when word. Gasoline is American for petrol, which motorists try to save.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasoline is fuel that drivers try to economise on, so the definition is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Tiny bit of second dish with onions?

parts.note: liver and onions is a classic British dish, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A diner asks for just a sliver of a second helping of something oniony.
explanation.walkthrough: Liver and onions is a traditional British dish; the question mark admits that the dish is defined only by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver is a small thin piece, a synonym for a tiny bit.

clue.text: Girl blocking grass track

indicators.note: blocking means the girl sits inside the grass word, obstructing it

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to sing
Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl stops anyone walking across the grass track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn but is the slang verb meaning to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short railway track off the main line, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: East German in wicked deception

indicators.note: in tells us the German word goes inside the wicked word

parts.note: impure means morally wicked
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: An East German is accused of being involved in a wicked fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is not a person from the GDR but the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a fraudulent pretence of being someone else, a deception.

clue.text: End of the dog's dinner it's eaten something rubbery

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the next word
eaten means the it word is swallowed inside the dog's dinner

parts.note: a bone is a dog's dinner
it is taken as written

explanation.surface: At the end, the dog has eaten something rubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' puts the it inside the dog's dinner; the end of 'the' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is hard vulcanised rubber, so it is literally something rubbery.

clue.text: Little devil spoken to, no tot to be deeply influenced

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: no here means without, so the tot is removed from the word for spoken to

parts.note: addressed means spoken to
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A mischievous child is talked to and told off without being given a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes ADD out of ADDRESSED, leaving RESSED. 'Tot' looks like a child or a small drink, but here it is the verb tot (up), meaning add.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impressed is to have a strong effect made on you, to be deeply influenced.

clue.text: Something piercing protective garment — without front, little good

indicators.note: without front tells us to drop the first letter of the garment word

parts.note: an apron protects clothes
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: A protective garment fails to stop something sharp, which is not much good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without front' takes the A off APRON, leaving PRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a spike or tine of a fork, something that pierces.

clue.text: Walks past something in library and avoids taking short cut?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a person strolls past a volume on a library shelf
the idiom means strictly follows the rules, never cutting corners

explanation.definitionFit: Going by the book means obeying rules exactly, and literally a walker can pass a library volume.

clue.text: Keep appearing at front of house with relation

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A relative keeps turning up at the front door of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost that haunts a place keeps appearing at it; equally a person haunts a place they frequent.

clue.text: Huge majority at election? Country is led badly

parts.note: land means country

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of is led are disordered

explanation.surface: A political commentator complains that the nation is being badly led after a big election win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ISLED into SLIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming victory in an election, the idiomatic name for a huge majority.

clue.text: Couple of punches achieved victory, they say, in personal encounter

indicators.note: they say tells us the words are to be heard, not read, so we want a soundalike

parts.note: a one-two is a pair of quick punches in boxing; won means achieved victory

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a combination and wins the bout in a face-to-face fight.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE-TWO said aloud sounds like ONE TO, and WON sounds like ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one is a meeting between just two people, a personal encounter.

clue.text: Amount possibly for misfit

parts.note: read as an instruction, odd signals an anagram and the letters after it can be rearranged to spell amount, so the answer describes this clue's words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a misfit counts as an amount.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: ODD is the anagram signal and MANOUT rearranges to AMOUNT, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd man out is someone who does not fit in with a group, a misfit.

clue.text: Tiptop agent about to enter vehicle heading west

indicators.note: to enter tells us one piece goes inside the other
in an across clue heading west means reading from right to left, backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: about here signals that the agent word is turned round

parts.note: rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A top-notch sales agent climbs aboard a bus going west.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed before one goes inside the other, which is why two separate indicators appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb and tiptop are both adjectives meaning of the very best quality, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: One subverts toil with repeated hesitation?

definitions.text: One subverts toil with repeated hesitation?

indicators.note: subverts means the letters of toil are overturned and rearranged
repeated means the hesitation sound appears twice

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An idler undermines work by umming and erring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subverts' rearranges TOIL into LOIT, then ER, ER. The whole clue also describes a lingerer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loiterer dawdles and lingers, hesitating repeatedly instead of getting down to work.

clue.text: Drink making bishop frisky

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy means lustful or frisky

explanation.surface: A drink turns a clergyman amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit, a kind of drink, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Difficult week in one part of the hospital

indicators.note: in tells us the week abbreviation sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a means one
a ward is part of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient spends a difficult week in one ward of the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with or embarrassing, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: County clique given first report of the season

indicators.note: given first places the soundalike before the clique word
report means the words are heard, so we want the spelling that sounds like them

parts.note: summer is a season
a set is a clique or social group

explanation.surface: A social group in a county is first to report on the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMER said aloud gives SOMER. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the south-west, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Decide to drink a port

indicators.note: to drink means the settle word takes the a inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to settle a question is to decide it

explanation.surface: Someone decides to have a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major seaport on Puget Sound in Washington state, a port by example.

clue.text: Extremely happy, given place in choice group

indicators.note: given place in means the happy letters are set inside the choice word

parts.note: plum means choice or best, as in a plum job

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to be given a place in a select group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes H and Y from happy; they go inside PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A phylum is a major taxonomic group of animals or plants, ranking below kingdom.

clue.text: Enjoy a wee dram without hesitation

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
a shot is a small measure of spirits, a wee dram

explanation.surface: A drinker happily accepts a small whisky the moment it is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wee dram' is Scottish for a small glass of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'like a shot' means instantly, eagerly, with no delay or hesitation at all.

clue.text: Winged ace with others somersaulting

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: somersaulting turns the letters of the phrase head over heels, so they read backwards

parts.note: et al, Latin for and others, means with others

explanation.surface: A champion flier performs aerobatics with the rest of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' turns ETAL into LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alate is a botanical and zoological word for having wings, a synonym of winged.

clue.text: He died, but first Bill suffered

indicators.note: first tells us the bill piece comes before the others

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man died, having first been presented with a bill he suffered over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ached is the past tense of ache, to feel pain, so it matches suffered.

clue.text: Source of inspiration to preach "The first shall be last and .'

indicators.note: the trailing and ... stands for 'and the last first', so the final letter moves to the front
the biblical phrase instructs us to send the opening letter of the word for preach to the end

parts.note: to orate is to speak like a preacher

explanation.surface: A preacher quotes the Gospel saying about the first being last.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and last letters of ORATE: the O goes to the end and the E to the front. The unfinished quotation 'and ...' implies 'the last first'. ERATO is one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, and a Muse is a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Runs into the French quarter rather slowly

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
a ghetto is a quarter of a city
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A slow walker meanders into the French quarter of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into LAGHETTO after LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is a musical tempo marking meaning fairly slow, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: Break of day has receiver of bread and wine in sanctuary

indicators.note: break of means the letters of day are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the stomach, or tum, receives food and drink, here the bread and wine of communion

explanation.surface: At dawn a worshipper takes communion in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break of' rearranges DAY into ADY. The surface suggests Communion, but the receiver is just the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: An adytum is the innermost sanctuary of an ancient temple, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Poor white called this? Ruddy cheek!

parts.note: ruddy means red-faced
neck means cheek or impudence, as in 'what a neck'

explanation.surface: Someone is offended at being called a poor white: what a cheek!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first, with 'called this?' as a link. Neck is British slang for cheek or nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory term for a poor white rural labourer in the American South.
